extraction.name: FLEURS: Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech
extraction.description: FLEURS is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language. FLEURS can be used for a variety of speech tasks, including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Translation and Retrieval. The dataset provides natural human speech and high-quality transcripts for each language with strong quality control. It uses a bottom-up approach of collecting spoken utterances for aligned segments, while most other datasets are aligned at a document level with automatic segmentation and alignment for segments.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna
extraction.publisher: Meta AI Research, Google Research, Carnegie Mellon University
extraction.citeAs: Conneau, A., Ma, M., Khanuja, S., Zhang, Y., Axelrod, V., Dalmia, S., Riesa, J., Rivera, C., & Bapna, A. (2022). FLEURS: Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech. arXiv:2205.12446.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process starts with the FLoRes-101 dataset, which contains 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into 101 languages by human translators. For each sentence in the 102 languages (101 counted in FLoRes plus English), three recordings were collected by three different native speakers, imposing a balance in terms of sex ratio of at least 30/70%, when possible. Each recording was evaluated by additional workers to assess whether the recording corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings were discarded, leaving between zero and three recordings per sentence in the final dataset. In the first version of the dataset, about 21.5% of the sentences are missing because none of the three recordings were validated. The speech sampling rate is 16kHz. The collected data was split into train, development, and test sets with disjoint speakers between train/dev and test, with a target ratio of 7:1:2. All segments are within 30 seconds.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: About 21.5% of the sentences are missing in the first version of the dataset because none of the three recordings were validated. The authors plan to fill these gaps in future versions of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: FLoRes-101 dataset, which contains 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into 101 languages by human translators.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The textual data preprocessing includes tokenization, normalization, and character-based splitting. The original raw transcript (SRC RAW) is preprocessed by applying NFC and FST normalization, lower-casing, normalization, and removing punctuations. Words are split into characters, and token boundaries are defined. Three versions are provided: the original raw transcript (SRC RAW), the preprocessed version (SRC NORM), and its character-based version (SRC CHAR), which should be used for ASR. All recordings are kept as they are, either from quiet or noisy environments, without any data augmentations (e.g., SpecAugment, speed perturbation, simulated reverberation).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset provides natural human speech and high-quality transcripts for each language with strong quality control. The transcripts are produced by human translators from the FLoRes-101 benchmark. The dataset is designed for tasks such as Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Translation, and Retrieval.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three native speakers per sentence, imposing a balance in terms of sex ratio of at least 30/70%, when possible.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to fill the gaps in the dataset in future versions. The dataset is publicly available via TFDS and Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The goal of FLEURS is to enable speech technology in more languages and catalyze research in low-resource speech understanding, aiming to build speech technologies for everyone.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset includes biases due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in Western European languages from MLS and VoxPopuli, leading to better results for these languages compared to others like Sub-Saharan African or South Asian languages. Additionally, languages with Latin scripts have a higher average Character Error Rate (CER) than those using Cyrillic in unseen languages.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has missing sentences (21.5%) in the first version due to unvalidated recordings. The dataset is limited to 102 languages, and some languages may have limited representation. The dataset is not suitable for languages outside the 102 included. The dataset may have biases due to the imbalance in the amount of pre-training data available for different languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: FLEURS can be used for a variety of speech tasks, including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Translation, and Retrieval. It is well-suited for evaluating data-efficient multilingual pre-trained representations of speech (and text). The dataset is designed for training, testing, and validation purposes in few-shot learning scenarios.
